scenario_prompt: Write a set of discovery call notes, in the buyer's own words, attributed to the specific people who said them, so a later document can cite this material directly. Context, from a fictional discovery call: the VP of Infrastructure said, 'We need a perimeter we can actually govern -- right now every VM is a snowflake.' The Chief Architect said, 'Honestly, I'd rather extend the incumbent's contract than gamble on a migration during an audit year.' The CFO said, 'I'm measured on cost-per-load and a clean audit, not on architecture elegance.' Write these up as discovery notes attributed by role, with a one-line context note for each. Return only the discovery notes text.
text:
**Artifact family:** demo or discovery material

Customer source material for this task: the three verbatim quotes supplied above from the discovery call. `PF-3.3` fires against those quotes only; no other source material was supplied, so every other term is judged by the deletion test alone.

---

# Discovery notes — verbatim capture

## VP of Infrastructure

**Context:** Owns the estate; raised the governance problem first, before any capability discussion.

> "We need a perimeter we can actually govern -- right now every VM is a snowflake."

**Current state, in their words:** every VM is a snowflake. **After state they asked for:** a perimeter they can actually govern. [PF-1.2 GAP: what the snowflake estate costs today — no VM count, drift rate, or remediation effort was stated on the call] [PF-3.3: "snowflake", customer's term, retained — VP of Infrastructure, discovery call]

## Chief Architect

**Context:** Named the audit year as the reason to defer, not the incumbent's capability.

> "Honestly, I'd rather extend the incumbent's contract than gamble on a migration during an audit year."

**Their stated position:** extending the incumbent beats a migration this year. The objection is timing, not the alternative. [PF-2.16 REVIEW (competitor): the buyer named an incumbent vendor; any written comparison against that incumbent needs confirmation before it ships] [PF-1.13 GAP: the audit window — start and end dates — was never stated, so "audit year" has no baseline]

## CFO

**Context:** Stated what they are measured on when asked about evaluation criteria.

> "I'm measured on cost-per-load and a clean audit, not on architecture elegance."

**Their two measures:** cost-per-load, and a clean audit. Architecture elegance is explicitly not one of them. [PF-1.13 GAP: current cost-per-load baseline — the CFO named the measure but gave no figure] [PF-3.3: "cost-per-load", customer's term, retained — CFO, discovery call]

## Unresolved before this document is sent

| Marker | Rule | What is needed |
|---|---|---|
| GAP: cost of the snowflake estate | PF-1.2 | VM count, configuration drift rate, or remediation hours — ask the VP of Infrastructure |
| Retained: "snowflake" | PF-3.3 | None; retained as the buyer's own term, sourced to the VP of Infrastructure |
| REVIEW (competitor): incumbent named | PF-2.16 | Confirm before writing any comparison against the incumbent the Chief Architect referenced |
| GAP: audit window undated | PF-1.13 | Start and end dates of the audit year — ask the Chief Architect |
| GAP: cost-per-load baseline | PF-1.13 | The CFO's current cost-per-load figure and how it is calculated |
| Retained: "cost-per-load" | PF-3.3 | None; retained as the buyer's own term, sourced to the CFO |
